initial.name: attribution_association
initial.description: Measure the association of one outcome field with candidate factor fields over one registered resource version: per-factor Pearson and Spearman correlations with seeded permutation p-values. The claim level is always `association` — these are correlations, never causal effects — and constant outcomes or thin tables are honest not_applicable results. Publishes the full factor table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this analysis belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the Point analysis rows.

initial.name: attribution_effect
initial.description: Estimate one treatment's effect on an outcome under an explicit identification design (covariate-adjustment or two-period difference-in-differences) with balance, overlap, and interference diagnostics and a t interval. The claim level reaches `causal` only when a design is declared and every diagnostic passes; otherwise the same numbers are reported at the `association` level with named downgrade reasons. Unmeasured confounding is never excluded by these diagnostics alone. Publishes the diagnostics table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this analysis belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the analysis rows (panel rows for difference-in-differences).

treated_value.description: Row value marking the treated group.

design.description: covariate-adjustment or difference-in-differences. Absent: the estimate reports at the association level with a named downgrade reason.

pre_value.description: Row value marking the pre period.

post_value.description: Row value marking the post period.

unit_field.description: Property grouping panel rows into one unit (difference-in-differences).

interference_band_meters.description: Interference band: controls with treated neighbors inside it trigger the spillover downgrade. Declaring it is required for the causal level.

interval_level.description: Interval level 0.8, 0.9 (default), or 0.95; recorded in the spec.

initial.name: attribution_explain
initial.description: Explain one outcome field with a linear model over candidate factor fields: standardized contribution shares, R², and variance-inflation collinearity flags. The shares explain the fitted model under its declared factors — the claim level stays `model-explanation`, and omitted factors or collinearity can change them. Same-source artifacts and exploratory factor choices are never independent confirmatory evidence. Publishes the full table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this analysis belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the Point analysis rows.

initial.name: catalog_register
initial.description: Register a workspace GeoJSON file or an online spatial query as an immutable catalog resource. Returns a versioned ref and feature refs for analysis and map_add_layer; online results include a bounded candidate preview, source and pagination. Stored bytes never change with the source. Retry returns the original publication without rereading a file or repeating a network request.

path.description: GeoJSON file path (workspace-relative or absolute); mutually exclusive with online.

online.description: Fetch and register Tianditu data: {kind:"geocode",query} for one address candidate; {kind:"reverse",point:[lon,lat]}; {kind:"search",query,bbox:[west,south,east,north] OR region:"administrative code",limit?:1..20,offset?:0..10000,level?:1..18}; {kind:"district",query,boundary?:boolean}. Search requires exactly one bbox or region; no default city. A center+radius query has no native form: derive the bbox with r in degrees — west/east = lon∓r/(111.32*cos(latRad)), south/north = lat∓r/111.32 (r_km/111.32 for degree conversion). Pull the next page by repeating with offset = the returned next_offset under the SAME name; that publishes the next version of the resource, so both pages stay addressable by exact ref. Coordinates use CGCS2000 geographic (EPSG:4490). Search defaults to limit 10/offset 0/level 12; district boundary defaults false. Requires a configured provider; mutually exclusive with path/crs.

crs.description: Source CRS of the file; defaults to WGS84.

name.description: Stable resource name; re-registering one name publishes the next version of that resource.

authorization.description: Authorization domain to publish under; defaults to the local domain.

retry_of.description: Seq of this session's original catalog_register `tool/call` to retry: returns the already-published version and never re-reads the path.

initial.name: catalog_resolve
initial.description: Discover registered resource metadata with search, resolve one exact resource version with resource, or search governed semantic definitions with query. Choose exactly one branch. Discovery returns versioned candidates; exact resolution returns stable feature refs and a RetrievalBundle. This tool does not search online data.

search.description: Resource metadata filters: {} lists current versions; {name?,query?,fields?,geometry_type?,crs?,bbox?,time?:{from?,to?},include_versions?,limit?,offset?}. name is the exact registration name; query matches field names/geometry types/CRS, not feature values. fields requires all named fields. bbox is [minX,minY,maxX,maxY] and requires exact native crs; no implicit reprojection. time uses ISO timestamps and excludes unknown validity. limit 1–16 (default 8), offset defaults to 0; include_versions defaults to false. Pages are live, not a frozen query snapshot.

query.description: Business-language query matched against semantic canonical names and aliases.

applicability.description: Optional applicability text filter for semantic search.

initial.name: create_goal
initial.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

initial.name: data_export
initial.description: Publish map data as immutable, fixed-version artifacts in geojson, csv (points), kml, or shapefile ZIP. Choose exactly one source: an exact resource/artifact ref, one loaded layer (must be ref-loaded), or the whole map (one artifact per loaded layer, with per-layer success and failure reported honestly). Exports carry data only — no map styles or camera. Retry returns the already-published artifact without re-reading the source.

ref.description: Exact resource/artifact ref (`res-…@vN` or `art-…@vN`); mutually exclusive with layer_id and map.

layer_id.description: Loaded layer id to export (map_get_state lists layers); must be ref-loaded. Mutually exclusive with ref and map.

map.description: Export every loaded layer, one artifact per layer; per-layer failures are reported, never hidden. Mutually exclusive with ref and layer_id.

format.description: geojson | csv | kml | shapefile. CSV carries points only; shapefile requires one geometry family.

retry_of.description: Seq of this session's original data_export `tool/call` to retry: returns the already-published artifact and never re-reads the source.

initial.name: data_import
initial.description: Import one workspace data file (GeoJSON, CSV, KML, or a Shapefile ZIP) as an immutable, versioned catalog resource and use its ref for map_add_layer and analysis. CSV coordinate columns, a missing or unrecognizable Shapefile CRS, and undetectable formats stop at needs_confirmation with candidates and a fingerprint; ask the user, then resend with the decisions and confirm.fingerprint. Imported coordinates normalize to WGS84; the registered copy is immutable. Retry returns the original publication without rereading the file.

path.description: Data file path, workspace-relative; the format comes from the extension or content sniff. Omit only for retry_of.

format.description: geojson | csv | kml | shapefile; omit to resolve by extension/content sniff.

crs.description: Source CRS for CSV/Shapefile (EPSG code or +proj= string); KML is fixed WGS84 and refuses crs.

encoding.description: Text encoding for CSV (for example gbk); defaults to BOM sniff then UTF-8.

lon_column.description: Explicit CSV longitude column; skips the column confirmation. Pair with lat_column.

lat_column.description: Explicit CSV latitude column; skips the column confirmation. Pair with lon_column.

id_column.description: Optional explicit CSV id column that becomes feature.id.

confirm.description: Confirmation from the previous needs_confirmation result: {"fingerprint": "…"}. Resend the same call with your resolved decisions (format/columns/crs) as normal parameters plus this confirm object; a changed file refuses the stale fingerprint.

name.description: Stable resource name; re-importing one name publishes the next version of that resource.

authorization.description: Authorization domain to publish under; defaults to the local domain.

retry_of.description: Seq of this session's original data_import `tool/call` to retry: returns the already-published version and never re-reads the path.

initial.name: decision_update
initial.description: Submit one plan update for the current analysis goal: your tentative interpretation (stays tentative), candidate methods, steps, and data gaps. Cite the goal revision and plan revision you are editing against (`map_get_state`-equivalent context arrives in the injected spatial snapshot). The update writes only the plan state — it can never change the user's goal, acceptance criteria, or recorded evidence. Conflicts (stale goal/plan revision) are refused; re-read the current snapshot before retrying.

goal_revision.description: Current goal revision the plan is written against (from the injected snapshot header/目标 line).

expected_plan_revision.description: Plan revision you are editing against (0 when no plan exists yet).

interpretation.description: Tentative interpretation of the goal; never promoted to user authority.

gaps.description: Array of { id, description, status: open|blocked|resolved } (≤ 32); repeated re-open of one id beyond the remediation limit is refused.

evidence_refs.description: Array of evidence seqs this plan cites; every ref must already be settled in the ledger.

initial.name: exit_plan_mode
initial.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

initial.name: forecast_fit
initial.description: Fit the selected linear, threshold, or quadratic-ridge model through the declared training cutoff and publish it as a versioned model artifact (the ref forecast_predict consumes). In-sample R² is reported but is not predictive skill — run forecast_validate against the baseline first. Models using concurrent features record them, and forecast_predict will refuse such models.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this analysis belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the historical Point rows.

time_field.description: Property holding each row's ISO event time.

block_meters.description: Spatial block size in meters (kept identical to forecast_validate).

baseline.description: naive (default) or mean — the baseline the model reports against.

model_family.description: linear (default), threshold (single feature split), or quadratic-ridge (explicit squares with fixed ridge penalty).

initial.name: forecast_predict
initial.description: Predict `horizon_steps` bins past a fitted model's training cutoff for the prediction-origin rows. Reads the published model artifact (method-version drift is refused), enforces feature availability (concurrent features are refused — future values are unknowable), compares against the baseline, and flags out-of-domain feature values and drifted feature means instead of extrapolating silently. Publishes the prediction table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this analysis belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the prediction-origin Point rows (feature values only).

initial.name: forecast_validate
initial.description: Validate a forecast honestly: fit through the training cutoff, evaluate on the last `holdout_steps` time bins (time-forward by construction), and compare against the declared simple baseline. Concurrent features are refused — their holdout values would not have existed at the cutoff, which is leakage. Reports MAE/RMSE for the model and the baseline, skill, empirical interval coverage, and per-spatial-block validation rows. Publishes the per-row table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this analysis belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the historical Point rows.

time_field.description: Property holding each row's ISO event time.

features.description: Up to 8 { field, availability } entries; availability is known-at-origin or concurrent (concurrent is refused here).

training_to.description: Training cutoff (ISO, exclusive): rows at or after it never enter the fit.

block_meters.description: Spatial block size in meters for the per-block validation rows.

granularity.description: day (default), week, or month — the UTC bin.

baseline.description: naive (default, last training bin) or mean — the comparison baseline.

model_family.description: linear (default), threshold (single feature split), or quadratic-ridge (explicit squares with fixed ridge penalty).

holdout_steps.description: Last k bins held out (1–64, default 4).

initial.name: geo_area
initial.description: Measure the geodesic area (square meters) and bounding box of a polygonal GeoJSON feature. Give EITHER `path` (workspace file; `feature_index` selects, default 0) OR `ref` (exact resource + feature refs). Pass `crs` for projected path sources.

path.description: GeoJSON file path (legacy branch; mutually exclusive with `ref`).

feature_index.description: Zero-based feature index for `path` inputs; defaults to 0. Ignored with `ref`.

crs.description: Source CRS for `path` inputs; defaults to WGS84.

ref.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

initial.name: geo_buffer
initial.description: Compute a fixed-distance buffer around a GeoJSON feature. Give EITHER `path` (workspace file, legacy first-geometry-feature semantics) OR `ref` (exact resource + feature refs; publishes an immutable, map-loadable artifact). Buffers in geodesic-equivalent meters and reports area, bounding box, and — on the ref branch — a `artifact.ref` you can pass to map_add_layer.

path.description: GeoJSON file path (legacy branch; mutually exclusive with `ref`).

crs.description: Source CRS for `path` inputs; defaults to WGS84.

ref.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

distance_m.description: Buffer distance in meters (positive grows, negative shrinks). Required unless `retry_of` is given.

steps.description: Number of circle approximation steps per quarter (higher is smoother; 1–32).

retry_of.description: Seq of this session's original geo_buffer `tool/call` to retry: returns the already-published artifact and never recomputes.

initial.name: geo_contour
initial.description: Interpolate scattered point samples (a numeric `field` on a points collection) onto a grid by inverse-distance weighting and extract isolines at the given break values. Input takes a workspace `path` (a points file) or a versioned resource `ref` (whole collection). Declares the method (turf IDW + isolines), the sample count, and the no-extrapolation limit: cells outside the sample hull carry no value.

path.description: Points GeoJSON file path (each feature carries the numeric field).

ref.description: Exact resource ref res-…@vN of the whole points collection (reads every feature).

crs.description: Source CRS for `path` inputs; defaults to WGS84.

field.description: Numeric sample property interpolated onto the grid.

cell_size.description: Grid cell size in kilometers; default 1, bounded [0.01, 100].

unit.description: Unit label of the interpolated field, for the record; default 无单位.

initial.name: geo_difference
initial.description: Subtract polygon B from polygon A. Each end takes a workspace `path` or a versioned `ref_a`/`ref_b` selector. An empty result means B fully covers A — reported as empty, never as a failure. With refs on BOTH ends the difference publishes as an immutable, map-loadable artifact.

path_a.description: Polygon A file path (the minuend; legacy branch).

path_b.description: Polygon B file path (the subtrahend; legacy branch).

ref_a.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

ref_b.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

crs_a.description: Source CRS of file A; defaults to WGS84.

crs_b.description: Source CRS of file B; defaults to WGS84.

initial.name: geo_distance
initial.description: Measure the geodesic distance between two point GeoJSON features. Each end independently takes a workspace `path` (with its own `crs_a`/`crs_b`) or a versioned `ref_a`/`ref_b` selector — never both on one end. Reports kilometers and meters.

path_a.description: First GeoJSON file path holding a Point feature (legacy branch).

path_b.description: Second GeoJSON file path holding a Point feature (legacy branch).

ref_a.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

ref_b.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

crs_a.description: Source CRS of file A; defaults to WGS84.

crs_b.description: Source CRS of file B; defaults to WGS84.

initial.name: geo_intersect
initial.description: Compute the geometric intersection of two polygonal GeoJSON features. Each end independently takes a workspace `path` (with its own `crs_a`/`crs_b`) or a versioned `ref_a`/`ref_b` selector — never both on one end, and a ref never falls back to the first feature. Reports overlap presence, area, and bbox.

ref_a.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

ref_b.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

crs_a.description: Source CRS of file A; defaults to WGS84.

crs_b.description: Source CRS of file B; defaults to WGS84.

initial.name: geo_line_of_sight
initial.description: Compute line of sight (visibility) between two points over a registered terrain grid (res-…@vN). Requires the surface's vertical metadata (datum/units/epoch — no default) and its accuracy budget (surface_sigma_m). Samples the sightline at the given interval with optional earth-curvature/refraction correction and optional building/voxel obstacles, and reports visible/blocked/indeterminate with the first obstruction, slant and horizontal distances, and the clearance uncertainty. A grazing sightline inside the error budget reports indeterminate, never visible. Pass layer_id to refuse when the displayed terrain version is not this one.

surface_ref.description: Exact surface resource ref, `res-…@vN` (registered point grid).

vertical_datum.description: Named vertical datum of the surface elevations.

vertical_units.description: Vertical unit; "m" is the supported unit.

elevation_field.description: Elevation property; "elevation" is the recorded default.

observer_height_m.description: Observer height above the terrain; 0 is the recorded default.

observer_elevation_m.description: Absolute observer elevation override; skips sampling the surface for the endpoint.

target_height_m.description: Target height above the terrain; 0 is the recorded default.

sampling_interval_m.description: Sample spacing in meters; 25 is the recorded default.

max_samples.description: Sample-count bound; 4096 is the recorded default. Exceeding it refuses instead of coarsening.

surface_sigma_m.description: Surface elevation one-sigma in meters; the clearance uncertainty and honest indeterminate band derive from it.

endpoint_sigma_m.description: Endpoint elevation one-sigma in meters for both endpoints; 0 is the recorded default.

refraction_k.description: Refraction coefficient with curvature=corrected; 0.13 is the recorded default.

buildings_ref.description: Optional building-footprint resource ref (Polygons with a height property).

height_field.description: Building height property with buildings_ref; "height" is the recorded default.

voxels_ref.description: Optional occupied-voxel resource ref (Points at cell centers with a z property).

z_field.description: Voxel center-elevation property with voxels_ref; "z" is the recorded default.

voxel_cell_m.description: Cubic cell edge in meters with voxels_ref (required with voxels).

control_points.description: Surveyed {id, lon, lat, elevation_m} points the surface must match before computing.

control_tolerance_m.description: Control-point match tolerance in meters (required with control_points).

layer_id.description: Terrain-preview layer id to check against; refuses when its revision differs from the computed one.

initial.name: geo_nearest
initial.description: Find the nearest facility to one demand point by STRAIGHT-LINE geodesic distance — this is explicitly not a road-network answer (use run_submit for network reachability). The facility end takes a workspace `facilities_path` (a points collection); the demand end takes `point_path` or a versioned `point_ref`.

point_ref.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

facilities_path.description: Workspace points collection holding the candidate facilities.

crs_point.description: Source CRS of the demand point file; defaults to WGS84.

crs_facilities.description: Source CRS of the facilities file; defaults to WGS84.

initial.name: geo_perimeter
initial.description: Measure the geodesic perimeter (meters) of a polygonal GeoJSON feature: the closed length of its outer ring(s). Give EITHER `path` or `ref`. Holes are excluded by design — this is the outer boundary length.

path.description: GeoJSON file path (legacy branch; mutually exclusive with `ref`).

crs.description: Source CRS for `path` inputs; defaults to WGS84.

ref.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

initial.name: geo_point_line_distance
initial.description: Measure the shortest distance (meters) from a point feature to a LineString feature — the true perpendicular/segment distance along the line, NOT the distance to either endpoint. `point` and `line` each take a workspace `path` or a versioned ref selector.

point_ref.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

line_ref.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

crs_point.description: Source CRS of the point file; defaults to WGS84.

crs_line.description: Source CRS of the line file; defaults to WGS84.

initial.name: geo_union
initial.description: Merge two polygonal GeoJSON features into one geometry. Each end takes a workspace `path` or a versioned `ref_a`/`ref_b` selector. With refs on BOTH ends the union publishes as an immutable, map-loadable artifact. Reports the merged area and bbox.

ref_a.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

ref_b.description: Versioned single-feature input: exact resource ref plus the stable feature ref to select (never defaults to the first feature).

crs_a.description: Source CRS of file A; defaults to WGS84.

crs_b.description: Source CRS of file B; defaults to WGS84.

initial.name: get_goal
initial.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

initial.name: interrupt_agent
initial.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

initial.name: job_kill
initial.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

initial.name: job_list
initial.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

initial.name: job_output
initial.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

initial.name: layer_set_state
initial.description: Batch-update layer presentation state on the session map: visibility, opacity (0..1), and display group per layer, as ONE revision (one undo). Give 1..32 entries [{layer_id, visible?, opacity?, group?}] (group null clears it; each entry sets at least one field). Layer data, order, and styles stay untouched — this never re-admits or replaces a layer.

states.description: Array of 1..32 entries: {layer_id, visible?: boolean, opacity?: number 0..1, group?: string 1..64 chars | null}.

expected_revision.description: Refuse unless the map is still at this revision (from map_get_state).

initial.name: layer_set_style
initial.description: Style one layer's presentation on the session map. Give exactly one symbol source — `symbol` (full SymbolStyle JSON), `preset` (a preset id like "marker-square-red-large"), or `auto` (deterministic palette color for the layer id) — and optionally `overrides` (per-feature patches [{featureIds, patch:{color?,sizePx?,opacity?,...}}]) or null to clear existing ones. symbol/preset/auto and overrides=null may combine in one call; symbol null clears the layer symbol back to auto. Heatmap presentations require an all-Point layer with no classification style.

layer_id.description: The layer id previously reported by map_add_layer / map_get_state.

symbol.description: Full SymbolStyle record (single: point/line/fill blocks; heatmap: radius/ramp). Mutually exclusive with preset and auto; null clears the layer symbol.

preset.description: Preset id (e.g. "marker-square-red-large" or "preset:fill-translucent-orange"); expands to a full symbol.

auto.description: true: use the deterministic palette color for this layer id (autoSymbolOf).

overrides.description: Array of {featureIds, patch} entries (feature ids from the layer data), or null to clear existing overrides.

expected_revision.description: Refuse unless the map is still at this revision (from map_get_state).

initial.name: list_agents
initial.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

initial.name: location_allocate
initial.description: Allocate demand points to candidate sites under a budget and per-site capacity: the documented greedy rule opens sites by marginal weighted objective (coverage/equity/cost weights) with capacity-capped nearest-site assignment. Unaffordable sites stay closed and named; capacity shortfalls and uncovered rows keep the honest partial status; absent weights select the flagged default scenario. Optional global mode enumerates the bounded declared affordable-site domain and reports its greedy comparison. Publishes the allocation table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this analysis belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the Point demand rows.

group_field.description: Property partitioning demand into equity groups; rows without it form the group "all".

sites.description: 1–64 { id, lon, lat, capacity, cost } candidate sites.

budget.description: Opening budget; sites above it stay closed and named.

mode.description: greedy (default) or global bounded exhaustive search over the declared affordable sites.

weights.description: { coverage, equity, cost } value weights; absence selects the flagged default scenario.

initial.name: map_add_layer
initial.description: Add a layer to the map container of the current session. Give EITHER `path` (a workspace GeoJSON file; WGS84 lon/lat by default, pass `crs` for projected data) OR `ref` (an exact catalog ref `res-…@vN` from catalog_register, or a published artifact ref `art-…@vN` from geo_buffer) OR `tile_url` (a key-free HTTPS XYZ tile template like https://tiles.example.org/{z}/{y}/{x}.png — an imagery overlay with no feature data) — never more than one. Versioned layers carry their data identity and display digest; imagery layers carry their normalized tile identity.

path.description: GeoJSON file path (workspace-relative or absolute). Legacy branch.

ref.description: Exact catalog ref (`res-…@vN` resource or `art-…@vN` artifact). Versioned branch.

tile_url.description: Key-free HTTPS XYZ tile template ({z}/{y}/{x} or {level}/{row}/{col}); no query strings or credentials. Imagery branch.

name.description: Human-readable layer name; defaults to the file base name, resource identity, or tile host.

crs.description: Source CRS for `path` inputs, e.g. "EPSG:4547" or a +proj= string. Defaults to WGS84. Ignored with `ref` (the version records its CRS); refused with `tile_url`.

layer_id.description: Stable layer id; re-adding an id replaces the layer.

initial.name: map_apply_patch
initial.description: Apply a conditional multi-op patch to the session map as one atomic change (one new revision). Each op may carry expectations (digests/absence/order/values read via map_get_state); a stale op conflicts with a per-op diff and NOTHING applies — re-read and re-decide. Repeating an operation_id replays its first outcome instead of applying twice. Deletes of already-deleted layers are never replayed.

patch.description: Array of 1..8 conditional ops: {kind:"upsert-layer",layer:{id,name,data,sourceCrs,opacity,visible,digest?},expect?} | {kind:"update-layer",layerId,name?,visible?,opacity?,expect?} | {kind:"remove-layer",layerId,expect?:{digest}} | {kind:"reorder-layers",layerIds,expect?:{order}} | {kind:"set-view",view:{center,zoom,wkid},expect?:{viewDigest}} | {kind:"set-mode",mode,expect?:{mode}} | {kind:"set-style",entries:[{layerId,style|null,expect?}]} | {kind:"set-aoi",aoi:{name?,ring}|null}. expect fields name what you read: {digest,absent,order,viewDigest,mode,aoiDigest}.

expected_revision.description: The map revision this patch was prepared against (map_get_state).

operation_id.description: Client operation id for idempotency; repeating it replays the first outcome.

writer_id.description: Registered writer to commit as; defaults to this session's own writer.

initial.name: map_draw
initial.description: Draw one point, line, or polygon feature on the session map from explicit WGS84 [lon, lat] coordinates — no file needed. `kind` is point (exactly 1 pair), line (≥2), or polygon (≥3; the ring auto-closes). At most 1024 coordinates; larger geometry belongs in a workspace file or a catalog ref. Re-drawing the same layer_id replaces the layer. For navigation-only place lookup use map_locate; to persist fetched data use catalog_register.

coordinates.description: Array of WGS84 [lon, lat] pairs; a polygon's first vertex may differ from the last (auto-closed).

layer_id.description: Stable layer id (default drawn-<kind>); re-drawing an id replaces the layer.

name.description: Human-readable layer name; defaults to the kind.

label.description: Feature label carried into the feature properties (e.g. an entry point name).

initial.name: map_fit_view
initial.description: Fit the session map view to exactly one extent source: `bbox` ([west,south,east,north] WGS84), `layer_id` (that layer's extent), or `aoi: true` (the study AOI outline). Derivation: largest integer Web-Mercator zoom whose projected extent fits a canonical 1024×768 viewport with `padding` (default 0.15) clear per edge; center is the bbox midpoint. The display projection (wkid) is kept. An unknown layer, unset AOI, or degenerate (zero-area) bbox refuses instead of guessing.

bbox.description: Extent [west, south, east, north] in WGS84 degrees; non-degenerate.

layer_id.description: Fit to this existing layer's extent (from map_get_state).

aoi.description: Fit to the current study AOI; refuses when none is set.

initial.name: map_get_state
initial.description: Read the current session's map container state: every layer (id, name, feature count, visibility, content digest), the view, the current revision (cite it as expected_revision when patching), the AOI, and the recent operation history (undo targets).

initial.name: map_locate
initial.description: Resolve one place name to coordinates for map navigation (read-only; nothing is registered). Without `bbox` returns the geocoder's single candidate; with `bbox` ([west,south,east,north] WGS84) returns bounded POI candidates with addresses — and honestly reports found: 0 inside an area the provider cannot match. Points are in the provider's geographic CRS (EPSG:4490 lon/lat for Tianditu, usable directly in map_set_view/map_fit_view). To persist or analyze fetched data use catalog_register.

query.description: The place name to resolve (1..256 chars).

bbox.description: Optional [west, south, east, north] WGS84 window: switch to a bounded POI search for multiple candidates.

initial.name: map_observe
initial.description: Capture a screenshot of this session's map at its CURRENT revision and return it as an image for visual inspection. Requires a mounted map client (an open map occurrence) and a vision-capable model; both are checked before the capture is submitted. The image binds to the exact map revision — pixel reading is observation, never measurement: geometry and values come from the geo_*/stats_* tools. `timeout_ms` bounds the client capture window (default 20000, max 60000).

initial.name: map_remove_layer
initial.description: Remove one layer (by layer id) from the current session's map container.

layer_id.description: The layer id previously reported by map_add_layer.

initial.name: map_save
initial.description: Durably save the current session's map: confirm the referenced resource/artifact bytes in the map store, then checkpoint the accepted session prefix. Returns a receipt with the covered sequence, the map revision, and each storage stage's independent status.

map_revision.description: Expected current map revision; a mismatch refuses the save before any I/O.

initial.name: map_set_mode
initial.description: Switch the current session's map container between 2D (`map`) and 3D (`scene`). The 3D scene is a local scene: it supports projected coordinate systems and renders extruded, draped, and elevated data.

initial.name: map_set_view
initial.description: Move the map view of the current session. `center` is WGS84 [lon, lat]. `zoom` follows the Web-Mercator scale convention. Optionally set the display projection `wkid` (supported values: 4326/4490 geographic, 3857/102100/102113 Web Mercator, or CGCS2000 zones 4534-4554).

wkid.description: Supported display WKID (default keeps the current one): 4326/4490, 3857/102100/102113, or 4534-4554.

initial.name: map_undo
initial.description: Undo one recorded map operation by proposing its compensating change as a NEW revision (history stays). Without undo_of, undoes the newest still-live operation (repeat to walk back). Another writer having changed the affected slice since conflicts the undo — re-decide explicitly. External artifacts and files are NOT rolled back.

undo_of.description: Operation index to undo (from map_get_state history); default walks the newest undoable operation.

expected_revision.description: Refuse unless the map is still at this revision.

operation_id.description: Client operation id for the undo itself (idempotency).

writer_id.description: Registered writer to commit as; defaults to this session's own writer.

initial.name: pattern_change
initial.description: Measure per-unit change between two ordered, non-overlapping sub-windows inside one observation window: comparison must start at or after baseline ends (time-forward). Units missing a window stay unknown — no zero-filling; sparse windows return not_applicable. Reports the forward-holdout drift and per-spatial-block deltas. Publishes the full per-unit table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this statistic belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the time-stamped observations.

time_field.description: Property holding each observation's ISO event time.

baseline_from.description: Baseline window start (ISO, inside the observation window).

comparison_from.description: Comparison window start; must be at or after the baseline end.

observation_to.description: The containing observation window end, exclusive.

block_meters.description: Spatial block size in meters for the per-block delta rows.

unit_field.description: Property grouping observations into one unit across time (for example a device id); absent means each feature is its own unit.

granularity.description: day (default), week, or month — the UTC calendar bin.

min_coverage.description: Occupied-bin fraction the window must reach (default 0.6); below it the tool refuses.

holdout_blocks.description: Last k bins held out for the stability drift (default 1).

initial.name: pattern_cluster
initial.description: Cluster time-stamped observations in space and time (DBSCAN over meters and UTC calendar bins): neighbors share both the spatial radius and the temporal radius. Noise points are labeled, never forced into clusters; too few points or a sparse window is an honest not_applicable. The forward holdout reports how many holdout observations a prefix core still reaches. Publishes the full assignment table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this statistic belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the time-stamped observations.

field.description: Numeric property the cluster summaries average.

time_field.description: Property holding each observation's ISO event time.

block_meters.description: Spatial block size in meters for the participation rows.

min_coverage.description: Occupied-bin fraction the window must reach (default 0.6).

holdout_blocks.description: Last k bins held out for the forward-fit check (default 1).

initial.name: pattern_flow
initial.description: Extract origin-destination flows of moving entities over a fixed cell grid: consecutive observations of one entity contribute a cell-to-cell transition, in-cell stays count as flows, and a chain gap above max_gap_bins breaks the transition instead of being interpolated. Sparse windows are honest refusals. Stability is the top-K Jaccard between the prefix (holdout bins dropped) and the full window. Publishes the flow table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this statistic belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the time-stamped observations.

time_field.description: Property holding each observation's ISO event time.

cell_meters.description: Flow grid cell size in meters.

min_coverage.description: Occupied-bin fraction the window must reach (default 0.6).

holdout_blocks.description: Last k bins held out for the top-K jaccard (default 1).

max_gap_bins.description: Chain gaps above this many bins break the transition (default 1).

top_k.description: Flows in the reported top table (1–256, default 16).

initial.name: run_cancel
initial.description: Request cancellation of one accessibility run by run_id. This is a request, not a verdict: the worker either stops at its next checkpoint (cancelled) or completes the work already done (the real outcome with the cancel request recorded). Query run_get for the adjudicated terminal state.

initial.name: run_get
initial.description: Read one accessibility run's durable status by run_id: queued, running, cancelRequested, or a terminal partial/succeeded/failed/cancelled/outcomeUnknown with its metrics and artifact refs. The query never re-executes the run; a timeout on the original submit does not mean the run ended — query it here.

initial.name: run_submit
initial.description: Submit an accessibility analysis as a long-running job: population-weighted network coverage over the exact registered resource versions you cite, with optional candidate-option comparison. Returns a stable run_id and operation_ref immediately; the computation runs server-side with cancel checkpoints. Query progress with run_get (it never re-executes) and request cancellation with run_cancel. Crossing extents must nest study ⊆ retrieval ⊆ support; a walk/bike/drive target without a priced network fails as METHOD_NOT_APPLICABLE instead of falling back to a straight-line buffer.

goal_revision.description: Current goal revision this run belongs to; a finished run of an older revision never overrides a newer goal.

population_ref.description: Exact population resource ref (res-…@vN) from catalog_register.

population_field.description: Numeric property holding each unit's population (the denominator).

facility_refs.description: Array of exact facility resource refs (res-…@vN).

travel_mode.description: walk, bike, or drive — the network mode the impedance prices.

time_slices.description: Array from morning-peak | midday | evening-peak | night.

study_area.description: [west, south, east, north] — results are reported for units inside.

retrieval_extent.description: [west, south, east, north] — contains the study area.

support_extent.description: [west, south, east, north] — contains the retrieval extent; facilities inside still serve across the study boundary.

training_from.description: Historical lookback window start; must end at or before the observation start.

entrances.description: Array of { facility, lon, lat } network access points. facility matches feature.id, else a string properties.id. Facilities without any entrance are excluded and named in run_get diagnostics (code plus facilityId).

capacities.description: Object facility id → maximum population served (hard cap; overflow stays uncovered).

barriers.description: Array of { from: [lon, lat], to: [lon, lat], kind: blocked|delay, delay_minutes? }.

candidates.description: Array of up to 8 { id, label, facilities: [{ id, lon, lat, capacity?, entrance? }], cost } — only these given options are compared (no global optimum).

weights.description: { coverage, equity, cost } comparison weights; required with candidates.

cost_budget.description: Total candidate cost budget; over-budget options are reported infeasible.

retry_of.description: Seq of this session's original run_submit tool/call: returns the already-submitted run and never resubmits.

initial.name: scale_ingest
initial.description: Copy one registered resource version (res-…@vN from catalog_register) into the distributed-scale chunk store as an immutable, content-addressed version (scl-…@digest). The version is chunked into bounded row groups with per-chunk digests and bbox indexes, carries schema/CRS/time/authorization metadata, and is the only thing scale_read and scale_scan consume. Ingesting identical bytes again returns the existing version.

chunk_rows.description: Rows per chunk; 2048 is the recorded budget.

time_field.description: Property holding each feature's ISO event time; its observed range is recorded.

initial.name: scale_read
initial.description: Run one bounded read against a scale version (scl-…@digest). kind=range reads a consecutive chunk window (from_chunk + chunks, capped by the row/byte budgets) and returns a resume cursor; kind=tile reads one extent-grid cell (z/x/y), pruning whole chunks by their bbox; kind=query folds a predicate (field, op, value) across the version. Returns counts, aggregates, cursors, and a capped sample — never the bulk rows.

z.description: tile: grid zoom (2^z cells over the version extent).

initial.name: scale_scan
initial.description: Scan a scale version (scl-…@digest) with a predicate (field, op, value) in a dedicated worker process: every chunk is digest-verified before scanning, progress checkpoints accumulate, and a cancelled call stops the worker at a chunk boundary before settling. On success the fixed conclusion (aggregate + capped sample as GeoJSON) is published as an immutable catalog artifact citing the source resource. retry_of returns an already-published scan and never recomputes.

retry_of.description: Seq of this session's original scale_scan `tool/call`: returns the already-published artifact and never recomputes.

initial.name: scenario_compare
initial.description: Compare the given candidate schemes (up to 16) against the status quo under explicit coverage/equity/cost weights. Every candidate stays in the output: infeasible ones keep their named reasons (overpromise, capacity-exceeded, over-budget) and no rank. Absent weights select one recorded default scenario that is flagged `default_scenario` — never the objective unique optimum. The sensitivity table re-ranks under the fixed weight sweep and reports whether the top candidate is stable. This ranks given candidates only; it is not a global optimum.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this analysis belongs to.

groups.description: 1–16 { id, demand } groups; demand is the coverage weight.

candidates.description: 1–16 { id, cost, served, capacity? } schemes; served lists { group, amount } pairs.

budget.description: Total-cost budget; candidates above it stay listed as infeasible.

weights.description: { coverage, equity, cost } value weights; absence selects the flagged default scenario.

initial.name: send_message
initial.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

initial.name: skill
initial.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

initial.name: stats_autocorrelation
initial.description: Measure spatial association of one versioned field: global Moran's I with a seeded permutation p-value plus the local LISA high-high/low-low/high-low/low-high decomposition under the declared multiple-testing correction. Constant fields and too-few-unit tables are honest not_applicable results; correlations are never causal claims. Publishes the full per-unit table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this statistic belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the observation units.

standardization.description: row (default) or binary weight standardization; recorded in the spec.

permutations.description: Permutation redraws (9–999, default 199); recorded with the seed.

seed.description: Deterministic permutation seed (default 20260924); same seed reproduces every p-value.

multiple_testing.description: fdr-bh (default), bonferroni, or none — applied to the local p-values.

initial.name: stats_hotspot
initial.description: Detect cold/hotspot concentrations of one versioned field with Getis-Ord Gi*: each unit's self-inclusive neighbor sum is tested by a seeded permutation, the declared correction applies to the local p-values, and the fixed 0.05 alpha labels hotspot/coldspot. Density and significance stay separate claims. Publishes the full per-unit table as an artifact.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this statistic belongs to.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the observation units.

standardization.description: row (default) or binary weight standardization; recorded in the spec.

permutations.description: Permutation redraws (9–999, default 199); recorded with the seed.

multiple_testing.description: fdr-bh (default), bonferroni, or none — applied to the local p-values.

initial.name: stats_zonal
initial.description: Summarize a numeric field of one registered resource version per zone attribute (or over the whole area): count, valid/missing, sum, mean, min/max, population dispersion, and — with a denominator field — the weighted mean and the sum-rate. Reads the frozen catalog version, publishes the full zone table as an artifact, and reports limitations beside every aggregate. Zero valid units is an honest not_applicable.

goal_revision.description: Goal revision this statistic belongs to (diagnostic bookkeeping).

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) of the observation units.

zone_field.description: Property whose distinct values form the zones; the feature property name "zone" is used when absent.

denominator_field.description: Positive denominator property enabling the weighted mean and the sum-rate; the feature property name "denominator" is used when absent.

initial.name: stream_advance
initial.description: Advance a stream workbench by up to 256 scenario batches (one step admits the next batch into the bounded intake, processes up to the quota, closes windows the watermark passed, and materializes bounded data gaps). Returns one additive summary: admitted, processed, duplicates dropped, backpressure holds, windows closed, late revisions, gaps. The layer folds the updated window projection and the resumable checkpoint.

steps.description: Batches to advance; 1 is the recorded default, 256 the cap.

initial.name: stream_materialize
initial.description: Materialize a stream workbench: export every settled window (closed, late-revised, and data-gap) at its current revision as one immutable catalog artifact, cite the scenario version it was computed from, and fix the layer as the final materialized state. Re-materializing an unchanged state returns the existing artifact ref — never a second publication. After materialization the workbench is closed: further advances refuse.

initial.name: stream_open
initial.description: Open a realtime stream workbench over one registered scenario resource (res-…@vN). The scenario is a FeatureCollection of wire events grouped by `batch` (properties: event_id, event_time_ms, value; Point coordinates are WGS84 lon/lat; a feature with offline:true marks its batch as source-disconnected). Requires an explicit tumbling window_ms and allowed lateness_ms — the watermark trails the max event time by that much, and windows close when it passes their end. The workbench is pull-based: nothing runs between calls. Advance it with stream_advance; fix its conclusions with stream_materialize.

stream_id.description: Stable workbench id; becomes the layer id. Re-opening one id replaces the workbench.

name.description: Human-readable layer name; defaults to the stream id.

lateness_ms.description: Allowed lateness in milliseconds; the watermark trails max event time by this much.

dedup_capacity.description: Distinct event ids the dedup window retains; 1024 is the recorded default.

buffer_capacity.description: Intake buffer bound; 256 is the recorded default. A full buffer holds the source back.

max_events_per_advance.description: Processing quota per advance; 512 is the recorded default. The slow-consumer bound.

max_open_windows.description: Open-window state bound; 64 is the recorded default.

max_revisions_per_window.description: Late-revision ledger bound per window; 8 is the recorded default.

initial.name: stream_pause
initial.description: Pause a stream workbench: subsequent stream_advance calls refuse until stream_resume. The intake buffer, windows, and checkpoint freeze exactly; the folded layer keeps carrying the stream status.

initial.name: stream_resume
initial.description: Resume a paused stream workbench: the source continues exactly at the frozen batch cursor and intake buffer.

initial.name: subagent
initial.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

initial.name: subagent_fork
initial.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

initial.name: terrain_add_layer
initial.description: Add a terrain-preview layer to the map from one exact catalog surface version (res-…@vN). The surface is a registered grid of points carrying elevations under `elevation_field`; vertical metadata (datum/units/epoch) is required and recorded — there is no default datum. The preview is a bounded decimation for 2D/3D display; run visibility analysis against the same version with geo_line_of_sight.

ref.description: Exact surface resource ref, `res-…@vN` (a registered point grid).

vertical_datum.description: Named vertical datum, e.g. EGM96, NAVD88, ellipsoid-WGS84.

vertical_units.description: Vertical unit; "m" is the supported unit.

vertical_epoch.description: Datum epoch or realization, e.g. "2010.00"; literal "none" for datum-less ellipsoidal heights.

elevation_field.description: Numeric property holding each grid point's elevation; "elevation" is the recorded default.

name.description: Human-readable layer name; defaults to the surface ref.

layer_id.description: Stable layer id; re-adding an id replaces the layer.

initial.name: terrain_slope
initial.description: Compute per-cell slope (degrees) over one exact surface version (res-…@vN, a registered elevation grid): central differences over the grid, meters via the local tangent plane, vertical units from the surface record. Reports min/mean/max slope and missing cells. A planar surface returns the analytic atan answer; the vertical datum and units travel with the surface version.

elevation_field.description: Numeric elevation property; "elevation" is the recorded default.

initial.name: terrain_viewshed
initial.description: Compute the area viewshed around one observer over a registered terrain grid (res-…@vN): a deterministic lattice of ground targets within radius_m runs the same line-of-sight core per target — identical sampling, curvature/refraction, uncertainty band, and refusal semantics — and reports per-target visible/blocked/indeterminate/outside with tallies. Off-surface lattice points tally as outside, never as invisible. The full table publishes as an artifact citing the surface version. Pass layer_id to refuse when the displayed terrain version is not this one.

surface_ref.description: Exact surface resource ref, `res-…@vN` (registered point grid).

vertical_datum.description: Named vertical datum of the surface elevations.

vertical_units.description: Vertical unit; "m" is the supported unit.

elevation_field.description: Elevation property; "elevation" is the recorded default.

observer_height_m.description: Observer height above the terrain; 0 is the recorded default.

radius_m.description: Area radius in meters, up to 20000 (the viewshed bound).

max_targets.description: Lattice target bound in [1, 512]; 512 is the recorded default. Nearest targets answer first.

sampling_interval_m.description: Per-sightline sample spacing in meters; 25 is the recorded default.

surface_sigma_m.description: Surface elevation one-sigma in meters; the per-target indeterminate band derives from it.

refraction_k.description: Refraction coefficient with curvature=corrected; 0.13 is the recorded default.

layer_id.description: Terrain-preview layer id to check against; refuses when its revision differs from the computed one.

initial.name: todo_write
initial.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

initial.name: update_goal
initial.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

initial.name: viz_aggregate
initial.description: Aggregate one registered resource version into a deterministic lon/lat grid and add it as a bounded display layer: per-cell count, or sum over one numeric field, classified honestly for the legend. The layer declares its display-aggregate identity (source ref, cell size, measure) — it is for seeing distribution, never for analysis math. Oversized resources stream feature by feature; identical inputs produce identical layers.

layer_id.description: The aggregate layer id to add (map_get_state lists taken ids).

layer_name.description: Display name; defaults to the layer id.

cell_size.description: Grid cell edge in degrees (positive, e.g. 0.5 or 0.05).

measure.description: count (default) or sum — sum needs value_field.

value_field.description: Numeric property summed per cell (required for measure=sum).

unit.description: Unit the legend labels for the cell measure.

max_cells.description: Cell cap in [1, 20000]; 20000 is the recorded limit. Coarser grid on refusal.

initial.name: viz_classify
initial.description: Classify one loaded map layer by a numeric field: breaks are computed from the layer's own rendered data (never invented), the legend derives from the same style version, and the map change folds through the standard commit protocol. Rates/densities classify the ratio over a denominator field. Optional time binding gives the layer a workbench timeline. Manual breaks require the exact statistic ref they came from.

layer_id.description: The layer id to restyle (map_get_state lists them).

series_identity.description: observed (default), forecast, or scenario — the identity the legend declares.

denominator_field.description: Positive denominator property; required for rate/density.

class_count.description: Classes in [2, 12]; 5 is the recorded default.

breaks.description: Manual breaks (with classification=manual); strictly increasing numbers.

breaks_source_ref.description: Exact statistic ref the manual breaks came from; required for manual.

encoding.description: fill (default) or size — size point encoding needs measure=total.

time_field.description: With timezone/time_from/time_to: enables the layer timeline.

timezone.description: IANA zone the timeline renders in.

initial.name: viz_compare
initial.description: Compare two loaded layers on one unified classification domain: breaks are computed from the union of both layers' values, and both legends share them, so colors are directly comparable. Per-layer re-classification of a shared ramp is exactly what this refuses. Emits one map change restyling both layers.

layer_b.description: Second layer id; must differ from layer_a.

field.description: Numeric property to classify on both layers.

series_identity.description: observed (default), forecast, or scenario — the identity both legends declare.

denominator_field.description: Shared positive denominator property; required for rate/density.

classification.description: quantile (default) or equal-interval; manual has no unified-domain semantics.

class_count.description: Classes in [2, 12]; 5 is the recorded default.

encoding.description: fill (default) or size — size point encoding needs measure=total.

time_field.description: With timezone/time_from/time_to: shared timeline binding for both layers.

timezone.description: IANA zone the timeline renders in.

initial.name: viz_create_style
initial.description: Compute a classification style (StyleSpec + LegendSpec) from one registered resource version: quantile or equal-interval breaks computed from the actual field values, or manual breaks that must cite the exact statistic ref they came from. Rates and densities classify the ratio over a denominator field. Publishes the style record as an artifact viz_classify can cite, and reports the real breaks, class counts, and missing counts — never invented ranges.

resource_ref.description: Exact resource ref (res-…@vN) the values classify from.

measure.description: total (default), rate, or density — rates/densities classify the ratio over denominator_field.

series_identity.description: observed (default), forecast, or scenario — the identity the legend declares so a forecast layer is never mistaken for an observed one.

denominator_field.description: Positive denominator property; required for rate/density, forbidden for total.

class_count.description: Classes in [2, 12]; 5 is the recorded default. Tied data collapses honestly to fewer.

breaks.description: Manual class boundaries (with classification=manual); strictly increasing numbers.

breaks_source_ref.description: Exact res-…@vN / art-…@vN the manual breaks came from; required for manual.

encoding.description: fill (default) or size — size point encoding needs measure=total.

time_field.description: With timezone/time_from/time_to: the temporal binding the workbench timeline uses.

timezone.description: IANA zone the timeline renders in (with time_field).

granularity.description: hour, day (default), week, or month (with time_field).

time_from.description: Half-open timeline window start, ISO (with time_field).

time_to.description: Half-open timeline window end, exclusive (with time_field).

initial.name: viz_density
initial.description: Compute kernel density over one loaded POINT layer: each point's density = the weighted neighbor count within `radius_km` divided by the circle area (个/km², or `<weight unit>/km²` with `weight_field`). Publishes the derived collection (feature property `__density`) as an immutable artifact — load it with map_add_layer, then classify on `__density`. Intensity is a display measure, never statistical significance; the value depends on the chosen radius.

layer_id.description: Loaded point layer id (map_get_state lists layers).

weight_field.description: Numeric property weighting each point (default weight 1 each).

initial.name: viz_export_kml
initial.description: Export one loaded layer's current WGS84 data to KML 2.2 (placemarks + ExtendedData properties) and publish it as an immutable, fixed-version artifact. The format is KML — never reported as a Shapefile; multi-geometry features export as their first geometry.

layer_id.description: Loaded layer id to export (map_get_state lists layers).

initial.name: workflow
initial.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

initial.name: working_directory
initial.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.
